answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by linking influence to verified work, rotating witnesses, and escalating bonds. Each identity completes unpredictable tasks and must maintain a signed history; copied agents consume separate collateral and reviewer capacity. A plume of trust rises only when unrelated witnesses agree, a terrace ledger records each milestone, and a wander limit slows rapid reward claims. Audits slash fabricated histories, making mass identities costly to sustain.
